INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

0 9 If this consumer wants to maximise total utility, which combination of goods would they consume? good S good T
What is achieved in monopolistic competition in the long run? allocative supernormal efficiency profit
The world’s largest pharmaceutical companies developed and distributed an effective vaccine to combat a dangerous virus. What can be associated with this vaccine programme?

options.A: demerit good and negative production externality
options.B: imperfect competition and positive consumption externality
options.C: perfect competition and negative consumption externality
options.D: public good and negative production externality

questions.questionText: A landlord owns a house which is rented to tenants. The tenants are required to pay the electricity and water bills. The landlord is required to decorate and repair damage to the house and its gardens. What is not an example of the principal-agent problem?

options.A: The tenants forget to switch off a tap when filling a bath and water overflows, damaging the floor.
options.B: The tenants have a party and their guests cause damage to the interior of the house.
options.C: The tenants leave the lights and the TV on when they go out for an evening meal.
options.D: The tenants park their car in the garden, damaging the grass and the surrounding hedge.

questions.questionText: The result of a cost-benefit analysis of a proposed government road-building project is that there will be a positive net social benefit of $50 million. Why might the government not proceed with the project?

options.A: The project would not be profitable for a private firm.
options.B: The project would cause negative externalities.
options.C: There is limited capital available for government projects.
options.D: There would be more who lost than gained.

questions.questionText: If the marginal cost of a good is lower than its price, allocative efficiency has not been achieved. What is likely to remedy this situation? production of price of the good the good

The diagram shows the supply curve of labour for two separate markets, X and Y. X wage rate Y O quantity of labour What explains the difference in the gradients of the labour supply curves?

options.A: Market X has a higher marginal revenue product per worker than Y.
options.B: Market X has a higher percentage of its labour belonging to a trade union than Y.
options.C: Market X has higher labour costs as a percentage of total costs than X.

questions.questionText: The table shows the main characteristics of employment in two occupations. occupation X occupation Y average annual wage $100000 $60000 number of weeks of annual leave 5 weeks 10 weeks average length of working week 48 hours 44 hours job security low high length of training course to obtain job qualification 1 year 2 years What can definitely be deduced from the table?

options.A: Those employed in occupation Y attach greater importance to job security.
options.B: Those employed in occupation X attach less importance to leisure activities.
options.C: There will be more competition for places on training courses to enter occupation X than occupation Y.
options.D: Occupation Y has more non-pecuniary advantages than occupation X.

questions.questionText: What is most likely to be the biggest contribution to sustainable economic growth in a developed economy?

options.A: a movement of people from rural to urban areas
options.C: an increase in the size of the population

questions.questionText: Which policy is likely to increase unemployment?

options.B: a significant increase in indirect taxes
options.C: the imposition of selective import controls
options.D: an increase in the public sector deficit

questions.questionText: What does the accelerator principle state?

options.A: Consumption is a function of the rate of change of income.
options.B: Income is a function of the rate of change of investment.
options.C: Investment is a function of the rate of change of income.
options.D: Investment is a function of the rate of interest.

A government adopts an expansionary fiscal policy to increase the economic growth rate. Which other main macroeconomic aims is this policy most likely to help? full stable current account employment price level surplus
Country X decides to devalue its currency to eliminate a balance of payments deficit. Why might devaluation have a positive effect on its macroeconomy?

options.A: Competitive pricing of exports may create employment potential in country X.
options.B: Foreign importers may depreciate their own currencies and reduce any advantage gained by country X.
options.C: Inelastic demand for imported raw materials may lead to cost inflation in country X.
options.D: Loss of import duties by country X may reduce government backing for trade promotion.

questions.questionText: Which cause of economic growth would involve the least cost for present and future generations of a country’s population?

options.A: increased exploitation of a country’s mineral resources
options.B: investment financed by borrowing from abroad
options.C: investment financed by high rates of domestic savings
